newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong lawmakers launch London lobby mission.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong lawmakers launch London lobby mission.

text.p: Hong Kong legislators launched a lobbying mission to London on Monday in a bid to spur Britain's political establishment to tackle problems facing the territory when China takes it back next year.

The five-member delegation would pressure politicians to raise the question of China's plan to disband the territory's elected legislature, and the anxieties of Hong Kong people about their future nationality and passport status, members said.
The mission comes just three days before Britain's House of Commons holds what may be its last debate on Hong Kong.
Britain is handing Hong Kong back to China in 232 days, ending a century and a half of colonial rule.

"We hope by our visit we will at least force them to think about this issue, however, briefly and also force them to think whether they should raise it at the debate and ultimately to see if the government can be pushed to do something more for us," Hong Kong legislator Emily Lau told reporters before leaving.

China, upset by electoral reforms in Hong Kong in the twilight years of British rule, has vowed to dismantle the Legislative Council and replace it with an appointed provisional chamber, whose members will be named next month.
The pro-democracy movement in the colony condemns the plan as a Chinese move to snuff out democracy.
The mission will renew efforts to press the British parliament to grant right of abode in Britain to more than three million Hong Kong people.
Hong Kong politicans have been urging Britain to grant full citizenship since 1984, when Britain agreed to return its south China outpost to Beijing.

The vocal critic of both Chinese and British policies also blasted Prime Minister John Major and Labour Party leader Tony Blair for showing little concern for Hong Kong -- they had so far not agreed to meet the Hong Kong delegation, Lau said.

A separate lobbying mission is under way by Martin Lee, a lawyer and the leader of Hong Kong's biggest political party, the Democratic Party, who is asking parliament to declare China's planned new Hong Kong legislature illegal.
Colonial Governor Chris Patten has also set off for London ahead of the debate, to outline Hong Kong's situation to political and business leaders.
